arxiv-2604-00781: Pentland and colleagues test neural-network emulators of virtual circuits for real-time tokamak control. Each circuit is a coil-current pattern that adjusts one plasma shape parameter on its own. In closed-loop simulations with the FreeGSNKE Pulse Design Tool, the emulators steered MAST Upgrade scenarios well and stayed robust under measurement uncertainty and varied update rates. The results support moving these real-time virtual circuits toward deployment in the MAST-U control system.
arxiv-2604-00881: Guastamacchia and colleagues study how large-scale fiber layout and small-scale disarray shape mouse-heart models. They build a detailed two-chamber model with a fiber field from mid-scale optical imaging as ground truth, then smooth the field to split large-scale layout from local disarray. Passive motion and activation barely change, while active motion is highly sensitive. Modest smoothing lifts pumping power, but too much smoothing or rule-based fields give unnaturally strong or weak contraction.
arxiv-2604-01281: Kounkel and colleagues build an uncertainty-aware neural network that finds eclipsing binary parameters from light curves, radial velocities, and spectral fluxes. Eclipsing binaries offer a direct route to stellar mass and radius, yet only a small share of systems have been fully characterized because fitting is slow and costly. Trained on synthetic data and robust to third light, spots, and gaps, the model handles 50 passbands and outputs uncertainties for all parameters. On about 200 solved real systems, it recovers masses and radii within about 20 percent.
arxiv-2604-01481: Ilaty and colleagues introduce DISCO-TAB, a system pairing a language model with a judge system tuned via reinforcement learning, for synthesis of data. Unlike prior methods using scalar feedback, DISCO-TAB grades output at four levels. It joins Constraint Discovery and Reward Shaping to preserve logic and resolve rare-class collapse. Across Heart Failure and Parkinson's sets, hierarchical feedback yields top performance. It achieves up to 38.2 percent improvement in utility over GAN and Diffusion baselines. It ensures statistical fidelity and robust resistance to membership inference attacks.
arxiv-2604-01581: Liu and colleagues study geo-localization where development uses only source UAV observations, with the satellite gallery unavailable until the model is frozen. They propose Orbit Completion Learning, which uses multi-view geometry as information with image-only deployment. OCL rebuilds each source scene using structure-from-motion and 3D Gaussian Splatting. A teacher aggregates the orbit into a target, while a student recovers this target from observations through distillation and contrastive learning. On University-1652, OCL achieves 57.85 percent R@1, best among satellite-free methods in eight of nine conditions.
arxiv-2604-01681: Chen and colleagues propose Agentic Fast-Slow Planning, a layered method splitting perception, thought, planning, control across scales. Perception2Decision shrinks scenes into ego-centric maps, then maps them to sign orders in the cloud with an LLM decider. Decision2Trajectory converts orders into paths: Semantic-Guided A* embeds language soft costs into standard search, while an Agentic Refinement Module adapts planner settings from feedback and memory. Tests in CARLA show Agentic Fast-Slow Planning lifts strength, cutting lateral drift by up to 45 percent and finish time by over 12 percent.
arxiv-2604-02081: Nehra and colleagues convert photon qubit encoding between polarization and time bin bases to link nodes. Quantum networks use platforms with other codes, and sharing entanglement requires matching basis codes. Their protocol converts polarization to time bin code, sends photons through a shaky fiber, then converts back for readout. The scheme carries a polarization Bell state across the fiber, turning infidelity into rate changes. The result offers a way to link distinct platforms for modular mixed networks.
arxiv-2604-02881: Gain, Singh and Ekbal study weight-space model merging for multilingual machine translation. Merging combines independently fine-tuned checkpoints without original training data. Merging works better when models share a target language, improving coverage over the base model yet failing to preserve peak language-specific scores. When target languages differ, results fall sharply, especially for shared-source and bidirectional settings. Fine-tuned models activate largely overlapping neurons instead of disjoint language-specific sub-networks. The tests use large-scale bilingual corpora.
arxiv-2604-02981: Pierce and three colleagues ask how pore-scale disorder shapes fluid stretching in porous media, which drives mixing of reactants, contaminants, and nutrients. They combine particle tracking in 3D-printed cells, plume simulations, and analysis. Velocity and shear measurements show deformation clings to solid walls at every disorder level, so near-wall flow drives stretching. Mean stretching grows linearly with time in ordered media and quadratically in disordered media, with roughly log-normal distributions. A random-walk model built on flow around one cylinder reproduces the random-media numbers.
arxiv-2604-03081: Qu and colleagues show how poisoned add-on skills can hijack coding agents that run third-party tools with system powers. Their attack, called DDIPE, hides harmful steps inside code samples in skill guides, so agents copy them during ordinary work. Across four frameworks and five models, it slipped past defenses in about 12 to 34 percent of trials, and disclosure confirmed four flaws, two now fixed.
arxiv-2604-03381: Gupta and Samaras test whether Big Bang nucleosynthesis still works in CCC+TL cosmology, where dimensioned quantities scale with a universal function. At nucleosynthesis redshifts the scaling reaches a plateau near 3, stretching cooling time, yet predictions survive when interaction and decay rates share the same scaling. Implementing the rescaling gives identical light-element abundances to within rounding, and BBN alone cannot pick between late-time baryon densities.
arxiv-2604-04081: Yi Zhou reflected on co-authoring a physics paper about AI with AI itself, as a case study in shifting authorship. Language models now act less like deterministic tools and more like virtual collaborators, forcing a rethink of human contribution. Zhou argued AI excels at structure and syntax, while the human must enforce physical logic, academic diplomacy, and peer-review foresight. The essay urges mandating publication of full unedited AI transcripts as supplementary material to protect accountability.
arxiv-2604-04281: Unlu studies how to pick a widened warm start when growing a small language model wider. Copying weights alone does not settle the choice, since full training states also carry optimizer moments and scheduler state. In a small TinyStories test he compares exact-copy, perturbative, asymmetric-reset and non-clone starts under matched budgets. Exact-copy starts win every short probe and the stochastic long runs, while the structured non-clone challenger wins long deterministic continuation. Preservation alone cannot rank candidates; the best signal depends on regime and lag.
arxiv-2604-04381: Subzwari, McDonald and Danagoulian compare two neutron detectors, GS20 and CLYC, for resonance transmission analysis in thorium safeguards. Resonance transmission analysis suits the task, but needs detectors holding timing and accuracy in intense gamma fields. In tests on a 1.50-millimetre tungsten target, clean and in a built high-gamma environment, CLYC beats GS20 on precision despite its longer decay time. GS20 discriminates neutrons from gamma rays only weakly, while CLYC offers strong pulse-shape discrimination. For thorium safeguards needing uranium-233 identification amid gamma backgrounds, CLYC-like detectors look more reliable.
arxiv-2604-04781: Nathanson studies intersections of product sets and sumsets in semigroups. For a subset A of a semigroup S, A to the h denotes all products of h elements. Intersecting a family of subsets before taking products always sits inside the intersection of the separate products. He investigates the product intersection set, the set of h values for which equality holds between the product of the intersection and the intersection of the products. The paper sets out problems and results on when that equality holds and when it fails.
arxiv-2604-04981: Röchner and five colleagues build an imbalanced dataset for studying quality control in next-generation sequencing, a key technique for reading DNA and RNA. Spotting quality problems across varied experimental settings stays hard, and existing repositories offer few quality-related features. Their dataset draws on 37,491 sequencing samples with two types of quality-related feature representations. The first type holds 34 features from quality control tools. The second type holds a variable count from eight to 1,183 features, derived from read counts in problem regions.
arxiv-2604-05081: Sellergren and co-authors present MedGemma 1.5 4B, a model in the MedGemma set for imaging and document reading. It adds medical imaging, including CT and MRI volumes and tissue slide images. It adds finding via bounding boxes, multi-timepoint chest X-ray analysis, and reading of lab reports and health records. The report details changes for modes in one design: new training data, 3D volume slicing, and whole-slide tissue sampling. Against v1, the new model lifts 3D MRI scores by 11 percent, and 3D CT accuracy too.
arxiv-2604-05481: Sepidband, Pham, and Hemmati test how much fault-location context language-model program repair really needs, across 61 setups on 500 SWE-bench Verified cases. File-level location dominates, beating a no-file baseline by 15 to 17 times, while line-level expansion often hurts by amplifying noise. The best recipes pair broad file context, typically 6 to 10 relevant files, with precise line fixes, and model-based retrieval beats hand-built heuristics.
arxiv-2604-05881: Nghiem and Wei give a mixed classical-quantum way to model Hamiltonians made of tensor-product sums. Known parts are solved on a normal computer first, then three quantum steps encode the Hamiltonian, and time growth runs by block-encoding plus quantum singular value transformation, a quantum math method. Cases where parts commute stretch to time-based rates, adding to past tools.
arxiv-2604-05981: Wu shows that a compact Kähler manifold whose holomorphic tangent bundle is uniformly weakly RC-positive must be projective and rationally connected. The result extends Xiaokui Yang's earlier theorem, which needed the stronger uniform RC-positivity. More broadly, any bundle with that weak property admits a Hermitian metric whose mean curvature stays above zero, and a quasi-positive version also holds in the same paper.
arxiv-2604-06181: Hadzidedic and four colleagues review 26 commercial digital weight management tools and survey 207 people using a real-life weight program. Adult obesity more than doubled between 1990 and 2022, and digital tools promise scalable, low-cost help through diet guidance, activity promotion, and counselling. The review finds the tools integrate self-monitoring, goal setting, and behavior-change strategies, yet miss social support, virtual reality, and adaptive personalization. Clients favor phone apps and fitness trackers for tracking progress, with varying comfort using digital resources.
arxiv-2604-06481: Gueriani, Kheddar, and Mazari build a hybrid deep learning model for Industrial IoT intrusion detection. It mixes ResNet-1D, BiGRU, and multi-head attention for spatial-temporal cues and attention weighting. SMOTE handles class imbalance during training on EdgeHoTset. The model reached 98.71 percent accuracy on EdgeHoTset, with inference latency of fractions of a millisecond per instance. On CICIoV2024, it reached nearly 100 percent accuracy and F1-score, with no false positives and fractions of a millisecond per instance. Across all metrics and sets, it outperformed prior methods.
arxiv-2604-06581: Laku and four colleagues model how trapped fluid blobs ripen inside porous rock, where curvature differences drive growth and events like snap-off and merging reshape the blobs. Their image-based pore-network model needs no idealized pore shapes, encoding capillary effects in local curvature-saturation curves. It couples flow, solute transport, and ripening together. Checked against earlier models and microfluidic hydrogen-ripening experiments over 15 to 24 days, it matched observations without tuning and resolved details a continuum model missed.
arxiv-2604-06781: Sun and four colleagues test a U(1)X vector-like-fermion model against Higgs signals at 95 and 125 GeV. The model adds a U(1)X gauge symmetry, three right-handed neutrinos, two singlet Higgs fields, and vector-like quarks and leptons. Scalar mixing in the CP-even sector yields two Higgs-like states near 95 and 125 GeV. Combining ATLAS and CMS strengths at 125 GeV with CMS and LEP excesses at 95 GeV, the model reproduces the 125 GeV signals. It also explains the 95 GeV excess, with new gauge and Yukawa parameters driving it.
arxiv-2604-06981: Prasad proves a global unique continuation rule for the parabolic fractional p-Laplace law with very rough terms. The result is new even for the fractional p-Laplace tool alone, while the matching local problem stays open even with zero terms. The short proof avoids extension tricks and Carleman bounds.
arxiv-2604-07081: Gatke, Schiller, and Müller give a detectability proof for large spread out non linear systems. That trait means a system state can be read back from its inputs and outputs with errors that shrink at an exponential pace. The authors prove the whole system gains the trait when each part has it, links are treated as outside inputs, and a small gain rule holds. They extend the proof to a Lyapunov form and derive local matrix rules.
arxiv-2604-07181: Opocher studies a policymaker's choice between measuring people better and sampling more people, when responses vary with hidden traits. He derives sharp worst-case bounds for assignment rules that use or ignore estimated latent traits, exposing trade-offs with policy complexity. He then gives a condition for a data-collection plan to be minimax optimal. In a development application, a business-skill proxy for targeting cash transfers raised welfare by 5 percent and halved the chance of welfare losses.
arxiv-2604-07781: Son and nine colleagues turn mixed three-dimensional car data into physics-aware graphs for neural networks. Inputs range from finite-element models and body-in-white shapes to CAD geometry and fluid meshes. The framework handles both sorting tasks and prediction tasks. Vibration mode-shape classification stays explainable when labels are scarce, while aerodynamic field prediction covers pressure and wall shear stress. The paper also advises engineers on which extra simulations or labels would pay off.
arxiv-2604-07981: Xiao and ten colleagues decompose long-context reasoning for language models into fundamental atomic skills. Long-context reasoning matters for complex real-world tasks yet stays hard, and research often misses the internal complexity of the task itself. Moving past a holistic view, the team splits the task into atomic skills and automatically synthesizes pseudo datasets targeting each skill. Empirical analysis confirms that skill proficiency tracks general long-text reasoning performance closely. Reinforcement learning on the pseudo datasets then sharpens atomic skills in hopes of lifting general performance.
arxiv-2604-08181: Dzhoha and Malykh propose Long-Term Embeddings, a high-inertia anchor for sequential recommenders. Modern transformer recommenders capture short-term intent but suffer recency bias, overlooking stable long-term tastes. Extending sequence lengths seems an intuitive fix, yet it costs much, and recent items still dominate attention. Long-Term Embeddings bridge this gap as a steady anchor. The paper also tackles a production problem: point-in-time consistency, since feature stores host only one live version of features, creating an offline-online mismatch at deploy or roll back.
arxiv-2604-08481: Li studies Lagrangian submanifolds in standard symplectic vector spaces through open closed string topology. For a closed oriented spin Lagrangian, he deforms the chain algebra of its based loop space by pushing forward moduli spaces of pseudo holomorphic discs along a string topology map. As a payoff, a Lagrangian with vanishing second homotopy group must carry a non vanishing Maslov class, extending earlier results of Viterbo, Cieliebak-Mohnke, Fukaya, and Irie.
arxiv-2604-08981: Kim shows that the equivariant unknotting number of a strongly invertible knot is bounded below by the torsion order of its involutive Bar-Natan homology. This bound mirrors an earlier bound by Alishahi for the ordinary number. In practice, Kim identifies five strongly invertible prime knots with at most nine crossings where the ordinary number falls strictly below that number. The result separates the new measure from its ordinary counterpart on real cases.
arxiv-2604-09181: Nayal, Wewer, and Lenssen present MixFlow, a training method that straightens the curved paths image-making flow models follow when sampling. It mixes a fixed plain source spread with a second source shaped by a signal that lines it up better with real data. The mix cuts path bend, so models need fewer steps, gain quality, and train faster. Tests show gains of 12 percent over standard rectified flow and 7 percent over earlier baselines at a fixed sampling budget.
arxiv-2604-09281: Gómez-Castro, Płociniczak, and Vázquez show self-similar solutions with constant finite mass exist for the time-fractional Porous-Medium Equation above a critical exponent. That range is optimal. Two types appear: compactly supported solutions in the slow-diffusion range above one, and positive solutions with heavy tails in the fast-diffusion range below one. Self-similar solutions in the linear case equal to one were already known via Fourier transform, and the authors discuss their properties and the limit as exponent tends to one.
arxiv-2604-09481: Chen and five colleagues measure the radio-frequency field-induced alternating-current Zeeman shift in multi-level highly charged ions. Pinning down the trap shift matters for precise optical ion clocks. The authors show it experimentally using highly charged calcium-14 ions. The sideways part is read via Autler-Townes splitting of Zeeman parts near resonance with the trap drive rate. The lengthwise part is read from a hyperfine jump that ignores magnetic fields in co-trapped beryllium ions, showing the shift's small effect with methods usable in other systems.
arxiv-2604-09681: Yang and six colleagues propose R2E-VID, a two-stage routing framework for elastic edge-cloud video inference. Existing systems adapt poorly to varied video content and shifting resources, wasting efficiency and compute. A temporal gating stage models consistency and motion to predict each segment's best route, splitting work between edge and cloud. A robust stage refines allocation, jointly cutting delay and resource use. Experiments show up to 60 percent lower cost than cloud-centric baselines, 35 to 45 percent lower delay, and 2 to 7 percent higher accuracy than edge-cloud systems.
arxiv-2604-09781: Baik and three co-authors tackle text-guided 6D pose rearrangement, where vision-language models fail to infer a goal pose. The team loops observe, check the instruction, propose a pose update, apply it, and render the scene, letting the model act as an agent. Three inference-time techniques matter: multi-view reasoning, object-centered coordinate visualization, and single-axis rotation prediction. Without fine-tuning or new modules, the approach surpasses rivals at goal pose prediction. Combined with motion planning, it beats Vision-Language-Action models at manipulation.
arxiv-2604-10081: Lee, Lee, and Lee treat image restoration and geometric matching as one joint problem with MatRes. Treated apart, the two tasks interfere when real photo pairs suffer both heavy damage and large viewpoint shifts. MatRes adapts at test time from a single low-quality and high-quality pair, updating only light modules while pretrained parts stay frozen. It needs no offline training or extra supervision. Tests across varied pairs show clear gains in both restoration and alignment over either kind of model alone.
arxiv-2604-10281: Suzuki, Chiba, and Wyse report stellar substructure in the Milky Way's outer halo toward Boötes, found in deep Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam imaging. The substructure is an excess of main-sequence stars beyond 30 kiloparsecs, spanning 100 square degrees. Comparing it with tidal debris from the Large Magellanic Cloud, they test first versus second passage. The overdensity sits where LMC debris is expected if the Cloud is on its pericentric phase 7 to 8 billion years ago, as second-passage predicts. First-passage cannot. Chemo-kinematical data must confirm its orbit and origin.
arxiv-2604-10481: Dihan, Awal, and Ahsan sharpen file retrieval for automated program repair tools that patch broken code. High recall matters, yet piling on files adds noise and slows the fix. Their PatchRecall method merges two hunts: matching the live issue to code, and mining past issues for edited files. A rerank step then trims the merged set to a tight final list. On SWE-Bench, recall rises with no big growth in file count, so repairs run cleaner.
arxiv-2604-10581: Singh and Lizarraga tune a Janus MoSSe silk sandwich for power from touch. Stretch pulls the interface band gap down past either part alone, showing tight layer coupling. The stack shifts its work function and grows a far larger dipole than its parts. Charge piles up at the boundary through Fermi level match and lopsided polarization. Output voltage and triboelectric yield jump across all stretch levels.
arxiv-2604-10681: Truong and Le defend language models against reasoning-level backdoors, attacks that plant malicious steps inside a model's chain of thought while keeping the final answer plausible. Their Critical-CoT method uses two-stage fine-tuning to teach models critical-thinking behavior: spotting possible backdoors and refusing to produce malicious reasoning steps. Experiments across several models and datasets show strong robustness against both in-context and fine-tuning-based backdoor attacks. The defense also generalizes across domains and tasks.
arxiv-2604-10881: Mukherjee, Asghar, and Brennen study counting queries with differential privacy on quantum-encoded data, where counting queries form rich dataset statistics. Answering such queries reduces to measuring the amplitude of an orthogonal state. For repeated basis measurements, counting-query privacy results improve on known results for general queries, showing privacy amplification through inherent randomness. For amplitude estimation, they bound global sensitivity, the amplitude change from adding or removing one item, and give a private version for counting queries. The methods can run on a quantum server for blind computation.
arxiv-2604-11181: Ghosh and ten colleagues tackle holograms made with binary light modulators, whose on-off pixels normally hurt image quality. Instead of binarizing a finished hologram, their step-by-step method enforces the binary rule at each round. Simulations and a mirror-device test show sharper contrast, better light use, and truer reconstructions than random superposition and Gerchberg-Saxton, at similar cost.
arxiv-2604-11381: Costa and Menendez improve quasiparticle nuclear Hamiltonians for quantum computing, targeting open-shell nuclei where proton-neutron correlations matter. They apply Brillouin-Wigner perturbation theory to the quasiparticle description of sd-shell nuclei. Energy errors fall below 0.2 percent against the nuclear shell model. A mean-field Hartree-Fock approximation of the non-quasiparticle resolvent then yields ground-state energies typically within 2 percent of exact shell-model results. That is a systematic gain over the bare quasiparticle Hamiltonian within reach of near-term devices.
arxiv-2604-11481: Kitaura reconciles structures with entropy growth through phase dynamics, transport shapes, and coarse models. Entropy depends on description level. A coarse field can grow ordered as structure forms, while the full phase-space description grows more complex through crossing. A Lagrangian-Eulerian map shows density amplification from the stretch Jacobian and collapse from tensor values. For cosmic fields, the tidal level matters at overdensity. The framework serves as a language for transport, unevenness, nonlocal effects, and self-ordering. The cosmos is the test case, but the language aims wider.
arxiv-2604-11581: Messing shows measurement error in LLM pipelines distorts annotation, tests, and benchmarking. Confidence intervals ignore spread from judge choice, temperature, and prompt phrasing, producing gaps that worsen with more data. He splits uncertainty into sources, separates variance shrinking with data from swings with design choices, and uses projections to cut error. Naive standard errors run 40 to 60 percent smaller than corrected ones, and 95 percent coverage falls as data grows while corrected coverage holds. TEE-guided pipelines shrink the gaming surface from 56 to 32 Elo, and acting on projections halves MMLU error.
arxiv-2604-11881: Anumarlapudi and eight colleagues report six new short-lived Galactic radio transients found with the Australian SKA Pathfinder's Variables and Slow Transients survey. Such sources, quiet at other wavelengths, previously numbered only about half a dozen, mostly toward the Galactic centre. Archival study splits the new sample into sporadic pulse-like emitters lasting minutes and flaring sources lasting weeks. Both classes resemble white dwarf binary behaviour, pointing to wide-orbit binaries for the pulsing kind and dust-obscured outbursts for the flaring kind.
arxiv-2604-12081: Kang, Voloshynovskiy, and Thalmann propose a context-aware memory architecture for social robots, holding textual and visual episodic traces, picking salient or novel scenes. Most robots rely on plain text-based memory, curbing tailored contact. Linking moments with single users enables social recall and more natural, grounded talk. On curated social scenes, this storage reaches a Spearman correlation of 0.506, above human level at 0.415 and beating older image memory models. In tests, fusion lifts Recall@1 by up to 13 percent over single-mode text or image retrieval, with real-time speed.
arxiv-2604-12181: Highsmith designs an online matching algorithm for markets where agents arrive over time and must match at once, such as placing children with foster homes or patients with rooms. His Sequential Equilibrium Mechanism approximates large-market equilibria to pair arrivals with objects, and is efficient in the limit, fair, and strategy-proof with probability one. Simulations show it can substantially improve welfare, and a lab-in-the-field experiment with real caseworkers is planned.
arxiv-2604-12381: Shilpi Srivastava and Shubhrangshu Dasgupta test quantum illumination against a realistic lossy target. It uses entangled light to spot faint targets in noise. The target sits at its own temperature, apart from its surroundings. The signal meets noise first, then the target. Each step is modeled as a beam splitter. Entangled squeezed light beats the best classical light on signal-to-noise ratio. It also gives a lower error bound for dim targets. The result bears on quantum radar and lidar.
arxiv-2604-12581: Maël Gonin and three colleagues review primordial black holes beyond the standard cosmic QCD transition. Such black holes could light up the dark ages of cosmic history. They are also candidates for dark matter. Phase transitions in the early universe shape how they form. The review focuses on the QCD transition within a recent microscopic model. Physics beyond the Standard Model shifts the cosmic equation of state. It also shifts the odds of black hole formation. Formed holes could feed present-day binary merger events.
arxiv-2604-12681: Robert G. West and four colleagues tune on-axis optical readout of InP nanowire resonators. Laser spot links to signal size and stability. Photothermal detuning maps the beam intensity profile. Heat-driven noise sets the detector signal. A noise model with shot noise and reflectance shifts predicts Allan deviation by spot. The best spot sits near the steepest intensity gradient. Raising laser power barely improves stability. Extra heat boosts heat-driven noise, canceling signal gain.
arxiv-2604-12881: Changshu Liu presents R2Eval1, a benchmark of 135 code reasoning problems from ten Python projects. Most benchmarks use simple generated snippets or puzzle-style solutions with only primitive types. Real projects carry compound and custom types with tangled dependencies. R2Eval serializes those types, keeping real data complexity intact. The result is a more realistic test of how models reason about code.
arxiv-2604-12981: Martinez-Rivillas, Ramos, and de Queiroz tighten the math behind Kan-style models of the untyped lambda calculus. They show a smaller starter package already recovers the associator comparison and bridge theorems of earlier work. They then prove explicit reify, reflect, and application formulas for the K-infinity model, with exact identities at every finite stage. The whole development is formalized in Lean 4.
arxiv-2604-13281: Zhang, Senoussi, and Verguts study how environment structure shapes cognitive flexibility, the ability to retain prior knowledge while carrying it to new tasks. They build a multi-task learning world with tasks combining two cue dimensions, mapped with graph-theory methods, and compare gating-based and joining-based attention models against layered networks. Richer environments improve both generalization and stability, and task connectivity strongly shapes both, with biggest benefits for attention models.
arxiv-2604-13481: Hall and Molina describe Monthly Diffusion, a climate emulator that models low-frequency atmospheric variability with latent diffusion at 1.5-degree grid spacing, building on a spherical Fourier neural operator inspired autoencoder. Designed to step forward at monthly mean steps in a data-sparse regime with modest computing needs, the model is presented with its design motivation, training procedure, and initial results. In short, it is a monthly climate emulator for the first AI-MIP, built to run cheaply where data are thin.
arxiv-2604-13881: Kono and colleagues design a flux-driven Josephson parametric amplifier from a SQUID array that pairs high gain with broad bandwidth near the quantum limit. The device reaches a net gain of 20 decibels with bandwidth around 50 megahertz, but its gain spectrum proves sensitive to weak reflections from impedance mismatches. Adding Fabry-Pérot interference to the input-output model reproduces those spectral features and separates device physics from environmental effects.
arxiv-2604-13981: Xiang and colleagues make object detection explain itself from within, rather than bolting explanations on after. PIEDet embeds class prototypes as explicit distinct units in a one-stage detector's label branch. Layered prototypes at varied levels learn scale-aware views. On ExDark, RTTS, and VOC2012-FOG, it lifts mAP by up to 4.8 percent over baseline while balancing explanation quality against cost.
arxiv-2604-14381: Bach and five colleagues tackle fair variants of combinatorial optimization, where the goal is a distribution over solutions that maximizes the expected worst case. An optimal distribution can need exponential support, so the team turns to the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm, showing a finite-layer ansatz can capture any spread over bitstrings. Their circuit solves the Fair Cut Cover well, beats classical approximations provably on some graph shapes, and beats them in tests. The result links dynamical Lie algebra work on QAOA to practical fair optimization.
arxiv-2604-14481: Ganesh presents many-body gravity, a modified gravity theory in a five-dimensional space-time-temperature setup where temperature shifts become metric shifts. Earlier work shows it matching galaxy rotation curves, radial acceleration trends, and Bullet Cluster lensing without dark matter. Here the theory yields cosmic inflation, while the author probes links between interaction, time, and gravity. A single massive particle, or non-interacting massive particles, makes time ill-defined under quantum field theory, so an interacting massless scalar field becomes necessary at inflation's onset, with entropy terms speeding inflation.
arxiv-2604-14581: Xiao's team of six tackles heterogeneous sequential recommendation, where diverse behaviors must reveal changing preferences for precise next-item prediction. Sparse data weakens results, clicks add noise, purchase gaps persist, and single-behavior augmentation misses fine detail. Their dual-channel system builds behavior-aware subgraphs for own transitions, then pools context with a cascade graph neural network. Contrastive learning then sharpens long-term and short-term profiles, fused by adaptive gating to pick next targets. Tests on three real-world sets show BDPL beating state-of-the-art models.
arxiv-2604-15081: van Gent Gonzalez and colleagues settle a dispute over the crystal phases of ferroelectric hafnia films. Standard probes struggle to separate the polar orthorhombic phase from a reported rhombohedral phase, yet device behavior hinges on which symmetry holds. Using 3D synchrotron diffraction maps of films in both phases, plus temperature and electrical checks, they confirm two truly distinct phases. The result clarifies the traits each phase brings to ultrathin devices.
arxiv-2604-15381: Gonzalez-Bermejo and nine colleagues test whether quantum machine learning can help track hydration from urine biomarkers collected by a smart toilet system. Framed as regression on specific gravity, conductivity, and volume, the study compares classical models, quantum regressors, and a new modular Quantum Sequential Model. Results sketch both the promise and the present limits of near-term quantum computing for health data.
arxiv-2604-15481: Wang and Camley analyze fracture in the finite Voronoi model, a nonconfluent tissue model whose cell borders mix straight edges with fixed-radius arcs. When cell-medium tension tops cell-cell tension, shrinking the time step unphysically suppresses cluster rupture, a flaw they trace to diverging detachment forces. A simple regularization plus calibration fixes the mechanics and can even flip how the fracture transition depends on cell shape.
arxiv-2604-15681: Haltmeier, Gruber, and Hwang tackle angular blurring in photoacoustic reconstruction from finite-size detectors, where standard fast methods smear images. Their self-supervised Noisier2Inverse method in the polar domain uses the known angular point-spread function plus a statistically grounded early-stopping rule, needing no ground-truth images. Tests beat unsupervised alternatives and near supervised benchmarks, staying practical for real finite-detector acquisitions.
arxiv-2604-15781: Wen and five colleagues ease reuse of picture-only charts with ReVis, a human-AI team-up. It reads a chart image into a broad chart tongue, then redraws it from that tongue. A shared tongue models knotty charts and backs both split-apart and redraw, while a live screen lets users drop in chart shots, check redraws, swap data, and tune looks. A 40-chart hall shows the tongue's reach, and a numbers test plus talks with 16 chart pros back its worth.
arxiv-2604-16581: Dihan and colleagues improve guessing for neural route tuning on vehicle routing. They modify random rebuild in the LEHD with cooling, swapping greedy choices with chance take-up. That take-up escapes local optima and tries a diverse solution space. They enhance policy tuning with many optima by adding beam search. Beam search slowly tries many good solutions while keeping variety. Testing plans and boosting by flipping and rotation, they find beam search and cooling-based rebuild best. Those changes greatly reduce the best-score gap across benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-16981: Constable and six colleagues release the LEOPs dataset of light-adapted eye signals for control, ASD, and ASD-plus-ADHD young people. Taken with skin electrodes and a handheld RETeval device in Australia and the United Kingdom, it holds 5,309 single-flash electroretinogram waveforms and 4,434 oscillatory-potential waveforms. The release adds stimulus code, demographics, test dates and times, diagnostic scores, and placement photos.
arxiv-2604-17181: Wu, Xiang, and Hu extend two principles for superconductors — the gene principle and the collaborative Fermi-surface rule — to bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7, superconducting near 80 K. Two exchange channels supply pairing: interlayer dz2 exchange via apical oxygen, and intralayer exchange between dz2 and dx2-y2 orbitals through plane oxygen. Bonding-antibonding splitting and the B1g symmetry of the dx2-y2 orbital make the channels cooperate into an s± state, with opposite signs on mirror pockets. Both maximize the beta pocket gap.
arxiv-2604-17481: Jha, Paudel, Parakh, and Subramaniam propose a quantum-boosted network design to protect microgrids built from small modular nuclear reactors. They mix secure quantum networking, quantum anonymous alerts, and quantum random numbers to guard integrity, secrecy, and privacy. To test it, they stage a traffic-analysis and spoofing attack that unmasks priority actions, forces heavy key use, and triggers harmful allow-or-block moves. The design then weighs privacy, uptime, and defense costs such as cover traffic, check delays, and key rotation.
arxiv-2604-17681: Guo and five colleagues propose FedCRF, a federated cross-domain recommendation method fusing knowledge across platforms while preserving privacy. Existing privacy-preserving cross-domain methods usually lean on shared users or items as a bridge, failing in non-overlapping scenarios, and handle global and local semantics poorly together. FedCRF uses textual semantics as the cross-domain bridge, transferring knowledge through federated semantic learning without overlap. Global semantic clusters on the server extract shared information, while a client-side FGSAT module adapts to local data and eases cross-domain distribution shift.
arxiv-2604-17981: Lovell and six colleagues present a method for emulating the halo mass function and other distributions in large volumes down to low halo masses. It costs a fraction of standard simulations. They select small regions of varied overdensity from the Quijote suite of N-body volumes run with varying cosmological parameters. Then they train an emulator conditioned on regional density and global parameters. Integrating over the density distribution recovers the global halo mass distribution, using just about 0.026 percent of the original simulation volume.
arxiv-2604-18581: Goldstein and three colleagues estimate non-Gaussian covariances by gauging small-scale signals to long-wave ripples via bispectrum and trispectrum estimators. They derive complete non-Gaussian matter gauges, including super-sample parts, from the squeezed spectrum and folded triple spectrum. Applied to Quijote runs, they recover fair small-scale matter values at the percent level with only 25 runs, similar to sample results from 5,000. This method greatly reduces runs needed for them, for guesses from survey data, stringent tests, and maybe studies without outside tables.
arxiv-2604-18681: Gavilan-Martin and ten colleagues show how periodic modulation can tune the spin-spin interaction in a hybrid atomic system built around an alkali-noble-gas comagnetometer. Shifting the electron spin direction against the nuclear polarization rescales the spin-exchange coupling, allowing its strength to be dialed down or suppressed without changing the system's intrinsic properties. The team frames the effect as a general tool for precision measurement and quantum memory.
arxiv-2604-18881: Wang and four colleagues present a proxy consistency loss for grounded fusion of Earth observation and location codes. Supervised learning with Earth observation inputs is limited by sparse high quality labeled data. Abundant geographic products offer proxies correlated with, but different from, the target variable. The method integrates proxies into a geographic prior through a trainable location code. Tests on air quality prediction and poverty mapping show gains over fusion with frozen pretrained embeddings.
arxiv-2604-19281: Sakib, Chisty, and Zhang argue that judging medical question-answering models by how close their wording is to a reference hides real risks, so they propose VB-Score, a check done piece by piece. It scores entity recognition, semantic similarity, factual consistency, and how complete the structured facts are, one by one. Reviewing three widely used language models on 48 public health topics from trusted sources, they find a wide gap between meaning-based scores and entity accuracy. A fluent answer can still get the facts badly wrong.
arxiv-2604-19481: Tripier and colleagues propose the walking cat design, a fault-tolerant quantum computer architecture for trapped-ion devices. Their blueprint includes a compiler, error-correction protocols, a micro-architecture, a fast decoder, and thorough simulations. The backbone is a cat factory, producing cat states distributed throughout the machine, consumed to perform logical operations. It rests entirely on low-density parity-check codes, a modern quantum error fix, with promising instances including a simple single-code version and a fast logical version.
arxiv-2604-19781: Burleigh studies confidence-based cascade scoring for grading student work, where small language models handle easier scoring tasks and escalate harder ones to larger models. The key question is which cases to escalate, and he tests verbalized confidence, asking a model to state a number alongside its prediction, as the routing signal. Using 2,100 expert-scored decisions from student-AI math conversations, he finds confidence discrimination varies widely, with the best small model reaching an AUROC of 0.857 while the worst gives a near-degenerate confidence spread.
arxiv-2604-20781: Wang, Pister, Phillips, Bissett, Higgins-Lavery, Wharmby, Sudmant, Hinrichs, and Bach report on making the UK Co-Benefits Atlas, which shares climate data. Atlases must address audiences and use cases, support guided exploration, and accommodate complex, evolving data. Over 10 months, their team ran 8 design workshops, drafts, 15 partner intro sessions, and review. These processes informed the development of the Atlas, with over 400 pages of visualizations and explanations. Looking back on their design process, they name five forces in atlas design: data, people, stories, context, and the atlas itself.
arxiv-2604-21481: Srija Anand and 12 colleagues test text-to-speech systems for Indian languages with pairwise comparisons across many dimensions, tackling the high variance of speech judgments across tongues. Using more than 5,000 native and code-mixed lines across 10 Indic languages, they test 7 systems and collect over 120,000 votes from more than 1,900 raters. Raters judge overall preference plus six dimensions: intelligibility, expressiveness, voice quality, liveliness, noise, and hallucinations. Bradley-Terry scores yield a multilingual leaderboard, with SHAP analysis explaining preferences, and reliability checked with strengths and trade-offs.
arxiv-2604-21681: Khirodkar and five colleagues present Sapiens2, a family of transformers for human-centred vision. Sizes range from 0.4 to 5 billion parameters, with native 1K resolution and 4K variants. Pretraining mixes masked image fill-in with self-taught comparison learning over 1 billion curated human images. The models beat the first generation on pose, body-part segmentation, and normal estimation, and add pointmap and albedo tasks.
arxiv-2604-21881: Li and eleven colleagues present SPAC, a system that automates FPGA-based network switches tailored to custom protocols and traffic patterns. Latency-critical services need minimal logic delay, while hyperscale training needs sustained line-rate throughput, so one fixed switch fits neither. SPAC offers a domain-specific language for protocol-architecture co-design, modular HLS switch components, and a trace-aware design space exploration engine with multi-fidelity simulation. Tailored designs cut LUT use by 55 percent and BRAM use by 53 percent, with latency cuts from about 8 percent to 38.4 percent overall.
arxiv-2604-22081: Staples studies an RL control setup splitting control into linked parts for sensing, heading, sparse memory, repeat commands, and local motion. The model is tested on a flat navigation task needing food seeking, obstacle dodging, and predator escape at once. In a six-seed test trained with Proximal Policy Optimization for 75 updates, the modular policy scores best among tested controllers. Its final score is -2798.8 ± about 964, ahead of two centralized controllers.
arxiv-2604-22181: Lobos and Rodulfo build a shadow framework for spinning black holes, linking quantum evaporation to plain geometry. A stable mapping change with a non-vanishing Jacobian splits bare mass from the inside. By shadow radius, they derive weak bending, Hawking temperature, and total glow. Applied to Kerr, Kerr-MOG, and Horndeski spaces, it solves setting mix-ups, showing distinct fields leave unique fingerprints. With M87* data, it breaks mass mix-ups, giving a robust tool for testing the Kerr idea and probing altered gravity.
arxiv-2604-22581: Cortild, Cartis, and Peypouquet study stochastic Krasnoselskii-Mann iterations for nonexpansive fixed-point problems in a separable Hilbert space. They prove convergence under far weaker variance assumptions than usual. Instead of a uniform variance bound on the stochastic oracle, they assume finite variance at a single fixed point. Under that assumption they prove almost sure weak convergence and derive expected, last-iterate, and running minimum residual rates. They also recover the best-known oracle complexity without a uniform variance bound. Applications cover stochastic gradient descent and two splitting methods.
arxiv-2604-22681: Kouzakov, Lazarev, and Studenikin study aimed neutrino spin sensing. A nonzero neutrino magnetic moment arises in the wider Standard Model with right-handed Dirac neutrinos. The result is spin oscillations in a magnetic field, showing as a dip in active cosmic neutrino flux on Earth and marks in elastic scattering. The authors study how any spin-flavor states sway recoil. Mixed left- and right-handed helicity states yield an azimuthal asymmetry in recoil angles. Math for scattering on electrons, protons, argon-40, and xenon-132 nuclei shows azimuthal asymmetry.
arxiv-2604-22781: Nayeri and Rezvani redesign how a temporal graph network gathers a node's past activity. It reads sequences both forward and backward and weighs distant context, to predict computer-network alerts sooner. Their aggregator, BiTA, keeps the host model's memory and message passing intact while adding multi-scale timing patterns that single-direction methods miss. Tested on real alert data, it beats current temporal graph models on ranking and accuracy in both familiar and unseen network settings.
arxiv-2604-23181: Ji and three colleagues release a 99-line homogenization code for lattice-skin plates, thin plates with lattice cores used in aerospace and in car manufacturing. Standard methods for lattice-filled volumes impose periodic boundaries in all three directions, missing free-surface effects through the thickness and biasing property predictions. Their open framework corrects this bias, stably extracting plate and shell stiffness matrices. It also extends to multiphase materials and steady-state heat conduction, giving designers a reusable base for light multifunctional structures.
arxiv-2604-23481: Nishimura and colleagues train a cell-nucleus classifier without hand labels, using spatial transcriptomics instead. That method pairs gene activity with nucleus locations in tissue images. Their framework converts gene patterns into cell types and transfers those identities onto ordinary microscopy images. On unseen tissues it matches standard supervised methods at finding and naming nuclei, despite using far fewer hand-labelled examples.
arxiv-2604-23581: Guo, Wu, and Yiu present AgentEval, a framework that grades multi-step agent workflows node by node instead of judging only the final answer. Executions become directed acyclic graphs whose nodes carry quality scores and failure labels, letting the system trace each failure to its upstream cause. It more than doubles failure-detection recall over end-to-end checks and, in a four-month pilot, cut root-cause hunting from hours to minutes.
arxiv-2604-23781: Meng and colleagues introduce ClawMark, a benchmark for language-model agents working as persistent coworkers across multiple days in a changing world. Its 100 tasks span 13 professional scenarios in a stateful sandbox where emails, calendars, and records evolve between turns, scored by deterministic checkers without any model judge. The best strict task success is only 20 percent, and performance drops after the first outside environment change.
arxiv-2604-23881: Ramos-Prieto and colleagues introduce the syncopated Bessel beam, a new exact solution of the paraxial equation from a sine-wave twist of the phase angle at the source. The imposed phase rhythm breaks symmetry, like musical syncopation, and triggers a shape shift that deflects the beam's path and moves its centre off the optical axis. An exact maths framework plus lab tests confirm built-in toughness and kept traits through travel.
arxiv-2604-24281: Piron and colleagues introduce the joint analysis pipeline for SVOM's ECLAIRs and GRM, the two wide-field instruments for prompt burst emission. The eclgrm pipelines at the French Science Center combine ECLAIRs and GRM data into products for broad-band temporal and spectral study. The paper presents pipeline architecture, activation after each onboard trigger, and workflow, plus statistical methods used by the pipelines and products created in real time or from event data. It also presents the eclgrm-ui interface, letting shift scientists monitor processing and optimize results interactively.
arxiv-2604-24381: Bieganowski and Schino prove existence and nonexistence of solutions to a fractional elliptic equation with a Hardy-type term and a mass constraint, in mass-critical and mass-subcritical regimes. A new Gagliardo-Nirenberg-style inequality drives the proof. The same results hold with the Hardy term removed and for a related curl-curl equation. The authors also pin down the threshold for the mass parameter dividing negative and zero least-energy cases.
arxiv-2604-24881: Yi, Mueller and Lee develop Latent Agents, which internalizes multi-agent debate. Debate improves reasoning but is compute-intensive, requiring long transcripts. Their two-stage pipeline combines debate structure learning with internalization. Internalization uses reward scheduling and length clipping. Across models and benchmarks, internalized models match or exceed debate. They use up to 93 percent fewer tokens. Through activation steering, they find internalization creates agent spaces. These are interpretable directions for agent views. Distillation makes harmful behaviors simpler to localize and control, with smaller performance drops than steering base models.
arxiv-2604-24981: Hozhabri Nezhad, Guo and Cheng explore speculative design to foster designer roles in open source. Open source often puts tech ahead of usability and design. Shortages of design skill and a developer-first mindset drive the imbalance. From forum study, they built two imagined societies: Husia, collectivist, and Reetar, individualist. In each, designers are prized in new ways and their work is used in new ways. A study with 12 practitioners, seven designers and five developers, found the societies provoked rich reflection on values and root causes.
arxiv-2604-25281: Devaraj and three co-authors combine CLASS surface sodium, LADEE-UVS data, and DIVINER data to study surface-exospheric sodium coupling. Surface sodium shows diurnal modulation, with daytime depletion and dawn-dusk gains, consistent with desorption. Exospheric sodium rises above low-albedo mare regions, whereas surface abundances show no mare-highland differences. Its structure tracks surface temperature and albedo, implicating thermal desorption as the dominant release mechanism. Release efficiency, rather than surface sodium abundance, governs lunar sodium.
arxiv-2604-25381: Tam extends his 2026 small-area frame to cross-classified stats from HB records. He adds PHIE, a Post-Hoc Inference Engine carrying HB-draw uncertainty to any cross-tab. PHIE turns MCMC draws through chi-square tuning into replicate weights, giving intervals in three tiers. Tier 1-E cells match tuning totals, giving exact intervals. Tier 2 cells gain near-nominal coverage via a Calibrated Bayes interval. Tier 3-NCV cells use a ratio interval tied to a linked variable. Cross-tab uncertainty comes most from sampling swings, and variation stays within bounds.
arxiv-2604-25481: Vivet and Arenas put forth a Hopfield-type linking memory with links tuned by glial gains under an entropy-tuned copy rule. The coupled neuron-glial motion always settles. At fixed points, glial gains give a softmax share over pattern likeness scores, yielding self-focus as new routing on the gain simplex. Under high memory load and clutter, the model lifts recall scores over old Hopfield motion and recent benchmarks. These results set out a systems frame linking glial tuning, rival resource sharing, and focus-like work.
arxiv-2604-25681: Breitling, Koerkamp, and Williams present SimdQuickHeap, a priority queue built for processors that handle several data items at once. Ordinary binary heaps suffer frequent cache misses and resist such vector instructions. The authors rearrange the QuickHeap layout, placing pivots side by side with elements grouped in buckets between them. The design keeps expected logarithmic cost per operation. It runs faster than the monotone radix heap and the superscalar sample queue in synthetic tests, and fastest on graph benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-25981: Bataille and Frontczak find closed-form values for several combinatorial sums. Their starting point is one identity connecting a combinatorial sum with Legendre polynomials. Some closed forms come through results on integrals of functions tied to Legendre polynomials. The paper offers a compact toolkit for evaluating such sums. The results cover several sum families rather than a single case.
arxiv-2604-26181: Wu and six colleagues present SWAN, an adaptive multi-mode network built for runtime shifts in input quality, input load, and compute. A quality-aware control assigns power among inputs within a user-set maximum budget. A gating module scales layer use to sample load inside that budget. A token-dropping module masks spare bits before spotting. On multi-object 3D spotting for self-driving cars, it cuts floating-point operations by up to about half with only minimal accuracy loss.
arxiv-2604-26281: Ulgen and four colleagues built DiffAnon, a voice anonymizer that lets users dial how much prosody, the melody and rhythm of speech, survives the disguise. Prosody carries meaning and feeling but also leaks identity, and older tools either drop it or fix the trade-off in advance. Using diffusion with classifier-free guidance, DiffAnon slides smoothly between stronger disguise and truer prosody inside one model. Tests showed a structured trade-off with strong utility and competitive privacy.
arxiv-2604-26581: Insley and three colleagues replaced PyCBC's binned histograms with normalizing flows for density estimation in gravitational-wave searches. Ranking a candidate event means comparing its statistic against a large background set, and histogram storage balloons with detector count, blocking analyses with four or more detectors. Flows cut storage by more than a thousandfold on third-run LIGO and Virgo data. Sensitivity held nearly steady, with loss under a tenth of a percent, while some detector combinations gained up to about 7 percent in recovered signals.
arxiv-2604-27681: Krönke and four colleagues quantify the Amazon rainforest's safe operating space under warming and deforestation. The forest may tip to savannah between 2 and 6 degrees of warming, while deforestation adds a simultaneous threat that can lower the tipping threshold. Under current conditions of about 1.4 degrees of warming and about 17 percent deforestation, more than a third of the forest is at high risk of crossing thresholds. The authors conclude the forest may already have left its safe operating space, urging climate action and an end to net deforestation.
arxiv-2604-27781: Cesarano and Monperrus treat the AI supply chain as a first-class study object across four layers: data, training, use, and a cross-cutting substrate. Across those layers they spot four built-in gaps that older tools miss: proof, versions, watching, and tracking. Current systems fall short on all four: hidden links, no rollback to known builds, silent decay, and lineage hard to trace. Counting a sample stack of 48 live open-source projects, they count 4,664 direct links growing to 11,508 knock-on units and roughly 392 million lines of code.
arxiv-2604-27881: Kuznetsov and Trofimov measure odd critical currents in near-one-dimensional aluminium wires pairing narrow and wide strands with unlike critical temperatures. They track currents against heat in zero field and against a field square to the base near the critical point. The field-tied switching current, marked by voltage on a stretch, proves non-local, hinging on electron flow near the junction line. Narrow- and wide-wire switching currents, measured and Ginzburg-Landau reckoned, differ sharply. A nonzero switching current survives past the critical field, defying theories.
arxiv-2604-28181: Ge and colleagues create synthetic computers at scale to train agents for long-horizon productivity work, where context lives in folders and rich documents. Each synthetic machine gets realistic hierarchies and artifacts, and one agent sets month-scale objectives for its user. Another agent then works across the machine until those objectives are done. Early runs on a thousand machines, each spanning thousands of turns, produced learning signals that improved agent performance on productivity evaluations in and out of domain.
arxiv-2605-00081:
Isaac David, Marco Guarnieri, and Arthur Gervais introduce alignment contracts for agentic security systems. These systems join language-model planners with tools that find, validate, and report vulnerabilities. The control problem is asymmetric: inside an authorized engagement the system should keep its full offensive strength, while the same powers must be denied outside the agreed scope.

A contract makes that boundary formal, defining scope, allowed and forbidden effects, resource budgets, and disclosure policies over observable effect traces. The authors give the contract language a finite-trace semantics, prove satisfaction is a safety property with finite violation witnesses, and develop refinement and composition rules for building contracts in modules. Checking admissibility is decidable, and the framework is instantiated for web-focused security work, with a Lean artifact checking the core theorems.
arxiv-2605-00581:
Nikita Zozoulenko and 3 co-authors put Newton boosting, the second-order engine inside the dominant tree-boosting libraries, on firm theoretical ground. Those libraries fit decision trees stage by stage, and second-order steps are their secret, yet global convergence of Newton boosting was poorly understood compared with first-order methods. The authors frame the problem as convex optimization with Newton's method on function spaces, allowing inexact steps.

Within that framework, ordinary Newton boosting provably converges linearly for smooth, strongly convex losses meeting a Hessian condition. For general convex losses, they add a gradient-regularized Newton scheme whose adaptive penalty scales with the square root of the gradient's size. That variant converges at a quadratic-in-denominator rate, matching first-order boosting with momentum, and is therefore a globally convergent second-order boosting algorithm. In experiments their scheme converged on problems where the vanilla method could diverge.
arxiv-2605-00781:
Jaeyoung Chung and four co-authors introduce Map2World, a framework that builds 3D worlds from user-drawn segment maps paired with text. Earlier generators often forced grid layouts and let object scale drift across a scene. Map2World accepts maps of arbitrary shapes and scales, which aims to keep global scale consistent while giving users more control over expansive environments.

A detail enhancer then adds fine surface detail without breaking the overall scene structure, by using global information during generation. The pipeline leans on strong priors from asset generators, which helps it generalize even with limited scene training data. In experiments, the method beats prior approaches on user control, scale consistency, and content coherence.
arxiv-2605-01181:
Han Lin Mai and four co-authors present a comprehensive first-principles evaluation of how light elements segregate to grain boundaries in ferritic steels and affect cohesion. They strongly influence alloy properties this way, but existing data are scarce and scattered. The team samples substitutional and interstitial sites in six model cases for eight of them using density functional theory.

At the same concentration, boron and carbon enhance boundary bonding, nitrogen, phosphorus, and hydrogen are mildly harmful, and helium, oxygen, and sulfur act as powerful embrittlers. Sampling both site types proves necessary, common site-volume criteria miss the deepest binding sites, and nearest-neighbor distance after relaxation controls the lower threshold for those energies. The dataset is freely released.
arxiv-2605-01381:
Burin Naowarat, Hao Tang, and Sharon Goldwater offer one frame for studying how neural models store human ideas such as topic, speaker, or sound type. Past work looked at linear concept subspaces from many angles, probing and erasing among them, without a shared test.

Their frame checks two things: containment, whether an idea lives fully inside a subspace and not outside it, and disentanglement, whether it stays apart from other ideas. Tests on text and speech models show the subspace itself may not be unique, and the tool used to estimate it changes both scores. The leading erasure method does well on both axes but fades on new data. In speech models, phone facts sit apart from speaker facts, while speaker facts resist being packed into a small subspace.
arxiv-2605-01481:
Noriyoshi Sukegawa trims a standard integer programming model for clique partitioning, the task of splitting a network into groups so that each group is fully linked. The model carries transitivity constraints, rules that force grouping to be consistent across triples of nodes, and they are legion.

Sukegawa pinpoints a class of these rules that can be dropped without changing the set of best solutions at all. The surprise is that each dropped rule still cuts a face of the solution shape, so by the usual test it looked essential. The smaller model shines on cases from correlation clustering, where edge weights are just plus or minus one. In computing tests the trimmed model beats the standard ones on such cases. The result is a leaner tool for a core grouping problem in data analysis.
arxiv-2605-01581:
Jinhao Zhang and seven co-authors shrink diffusion policies for robot control by looking at them through frequency glasses. Action paths are smooth, so nearly all their energy sits in a few low modes of the cosine transform. The team show the best denoiser's error is capped by that low band's size plus the leftover high-frequency energy.

Error therefore flattens after very few denoising steps, and action cleanup needs a far simpler model than image generation does. Their Hyper-DP3 policy pairs a light mixer decoder with two-step sampling, at pocket scale. Synthetic tests back the theory. Across two simulation suites, dexterous hand tasks, and real-world trials, the tiny policy posts state-of-the-art scores with under one percent of the parameters of prior 3D diffusion policies and much lower delay.
arxiv-2605-01981:
Zhuoqi Liu and colleagues study glowing gas clouds around bright quasars at redshifts near one, when the universe was younger. Gas moving between galaxies and their surroundings shapes how galaxies grow, and quasar light can make that gas visible as giant nebulae. The team combines data on thirty quasars from the CUBS and MUSEQuBES surveys.

Extended oxygen emission was found around twenty-seven quasars. The authors sort the nebulae into three shape and motion types: large irregular systems often tied to interactions, compact clouds near the host galaxy, and complex cases of unclear origin. For ten nebulae, a measured link to nearby group galaxies was significant, mostly among the large irregular systems.
arxiv-2605-02281:
Yunsung Kim, Hansol Lee, Candace Thille, and Chris Piech study whether a light, randomised course feedback method is linked to better student experience at scale. Asking for feedback often can lower participation and thoughtfulness. High-Resolution Course Feedback instead surveys each student a few times per term in randomly chosen weeks, aiming for timely and thoughtful replies without heavy burden.

Earlier work showed instructors find the feedback helpful. This observational study covers 103 course offerings and more than twenty-four thousand enrolments over four years, across many universities in the full paper. The authors examine whether use of the method tracks measurable gains in course experience, moving beyond instructor impressions to student outcomes.
arxiv-2605-02481:
P. Leguina López and nine co-authors speed up a core physics calculation by moving it onto a specialized chip array. Event generators for particle physics must score the same matrix element at many points, a task that grows heavy as the Large Hadron Collider moves to higher output. Their target platform is an AMD Versal AI Engine array, whose tiles each hold very little program memory.

To fit that limit, the team split the work into a five-stage cascade pipeline. Eighty such pipelines run across the chip's four hundred tiles and pass work through a token protocol. Projected throughput reaches about a million evaluations per second at modest power, many times faster than a single standard core, with a large gain in energy per result.
arxiv-2605-02681:
Sebastian Benthall and Alan Lujan define two new classes of causal models for decision-making agents, motivated by the economics of computing systems. Such systems have subsystems, and agents inside them face built-in limits on cognitive resources and discount future value. Standard causal influence models state links between variables and payoffs, but leave some of this structure out.

Their structural causal decision models add constrained decisions, where an agent's options can be limited by earlier causes, and open root variables with no assigned distribution. The models compose well, a property the authors prove useful. A decision process is then a repeating version with a discount variable. It is strictly more expressive than the standard partially observable decision model, because it does not assume rational belief formation and can model memory formation itself.
arxiv-2605-02781:
Cyril Houdayer and Amine Marrakchi prove a uniqueness result for a class of flows on a famous object in operator algebra, the hyperfinite type II-1 factor. A flow is a continuous action of the real line, and an almost periodic outer flow with full spectrum is the case in question. Such flows are the noncommutative cousins of rotations and other rigid motions.

The authors show any such flow has the Rokhlin property, a strong approximation trait, and therefore is unique up to cocycle conjugacy, meaning any two differ only by a controlled twist. The proof leans on a perturbation result for cocycles of amenable equivalence relations of type III. A side result follows: every almost periodic factor of type III-1 with separable predual carries an extremal almost periodic faithful normal state.
arxiv-2605-02981:
Johannes Fiedler studies how van der Waals forces change when the interacting systems are allowed to react back on their own light. Dispersion forces are usually derived with each system's internal spectrum held fixed. Fiedler relaxes that assumption inside macroscopic quantum electrodynamics, letting excitation energies and transition strengths respond to the interaction itself, with both self-energy effects and mutual influence included.

A minimal three-level model carries the analysis. One-sided self-energy effects turn out to be short-ranged, but fully self-consistent backaction can reshape the effective force substantially and at long range. The cause is a coherent build-up of repeated photon-mediated scattering between the partners. The results mark a limit of standard perturbative treatments with fixed spectra, and name few-level systems as a clean test bed.
arxiv-2605-03281:
Jonathan Muhire builds donor-aware benchmarks for classifying inflammatory bowel disease from single-cell RNA data. Splitting cells at random leaks donors across training and test sets, inflating scores through pseudoreplication, so honest evaluation must split by donor instead.

Across two cohorts for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, Muhire compares cell-type composition features with two learned embeddings. Stratified composition scored strongly, and a structured network method led in colon tissue, while linear models won in the terminal ileum. Transfer between diseases worked in one direction only. Careful feature construction proved central to both accuracy and stability.
arxiv-2605-03681:
Philippe Bouafia computes the magnitude of compact real trees, where magnitude is a numerical invariant of a metric space meant to capture its effective size. For a tree, the answer turns out to depend only on total length: magnitude equals one plus half the length, even when length is infinite. No finer geometric detail survives in that number.

Diversity tells a richer story. Bouafia shows that diversity-maximizing measures on compact real trees are more sensitive to branching, concentrating toward the leaves, with supports containing no branch points. In the finite case, maximum diversity on a weighted tree can be computed in polynomial time, making the finer invariant practical as well.
arxiv-2605-03881:
Ricardo Alonzo Fernandez Salguero offers a formal critique of treating government spending as a single aggregate number in the IS-LM-BP, or Mundell-Fleming, framework. Real fiscal policy mixes current purchases, public investment, and transfers to varied households. He shows the aggregate variable suffices for output analysis only under one strict condition. Every instrument must move output by the same margin.

The paper proves that condition. It derives multipliers weighted by composition and names the resulting aggregation bias. It extends the open-economy model to fiscal composition, public capital, debt dynamics, and risk-premium effects. A computing exercise confirms the argument holds together. The exercise uses basic checks, derivative tests, accounting identities, and counterexamples. It also uses Monte Carlo runs and stress tests. The point is methodological, and it is aimed at how fiscal policy gets modeled.
arxiv-2605-04181:
Rishad Shahmurov studies a possible route to blow-up, where values grow without bound in finite time, in a swirling flow that is symmetric around an axis. The flow sits in a repeating cylinder, and a symmetry in the starting state fixes the wall point where key gradients are measured.

He builds a detailed packet description at the side wall and derives estimates for how the packet couples to the core of the flow. Under a set of stated assumptions, those estimates force the comparison values to blow up. Shahmurov is clear that this is a conditional test, not yet a proof for one full smooth flow.
arxiv-2605-04481:
Batu Candan and Simone Servadio design a guidance system for a spacecraft using a weak, fuel-saving thruster to meet another, uncooperative craft. The most fuel-efficient control switches abruptly on and off, which makes it fragile when position estimates are noisy or sensors misbehave.

Their architecture lets navigation confidence steer the controller directly. A filter estimates the relative motion, with an inflation step that discounts doubtful readings. A combined score then adjusts a smoothing setting in the solver. When confidence drops, control relaxes into a conservative smooth regime; when sensing recovers, it returns to efficient switching. Tests under severe sensor loss favour the coupled design.
arxiv-2605-04881:
Emanuele Donno and five co-authors compare two ways of merging a dynamical model with noisy, partial observations, a task called data assimilation. One method, DATO, works with transfer operators from classical theory. The other, QMDA, borrows its machinery from quantum mechanics instead.

The team first writes both methods in a shared operator language, making their handling of uncertainty and updates directly comparable. They then test each on benchmark systems under noisy, sparse, and partly observed conditions. Despite their shared roots, the methods behave as distinct paradigms, with different strengths in clarity, robustness, and scale, and the study maps where each works best.
arxiv-2605-04981:
Santiago Llorens and three co-authors solve a fault-finding problem for quantum devices arranged in a series. Each device should apply the same unitary operation, but some unknown number may apply a different, unknown one instead. Reliable quantum computing depends on identifying such faulty hardware exactly, with no errors tolerated.

Using representation theory, the authors model total ignorance about the wrong operations and study a zero-error identification protocol. For one and two faulty devices they derive the best possible success chance, which surprisingly does not depend on how many devices are in the series. A simple protocol using helper systems reaches that limit and lets each device be tested separately.
arxiv-2605-05281:
D Singh and three co-authors present an exact black hole solution in anti-de Sitter space combining a Kalb-Ramond field with nonlinear electrodynamics, then work out its extended thermodynamics. The geometry has inner and outer horizons that merge at a critical magnetic monopole charge, beyond which no black hole exists. Turning off the Lorentz-violating parameters recovers several known black hole families as special cases.

Computing temperature, entropy, heat capacity, and Gibbs free energy shows the nonlinear source changes behaviour in striking ways. Temperature can be non-monotonic, entropy departs from the usual area law, and the free energy shows swallow-tail patterns signalling first-order phase transitions. The authors also derive the extended first law and Smarr relation and confirm both hold.
arxiv-2605-05481:
Improving a reinforcement learning policy safely is a chicken-and-egg problem: the value estimates must fit the new policy, whose data cannot be sampled yet. Dillon Sandhu and Ronald Parr propose Approximate Next Policy Sampling as a way out. Instead of shrinking the policy update, they reshape the training data to resemble what the next policy would gather.

Their SV-API algorithm holds the target policy fixed while a behavior policy collects fitting experience. Only a proven convergence test lets the update commit. Applied to PPO, the method matched or beat standard results while allowing much larger policy updates.
arxiv-2605-05781:
Unified multimodal models often keep their reading and making halves apart, and the halves barely help each other. Zeyu Liu and co-authors propose post-training that wires reading into making as a guide. Their framework, UNO, treats captioning and visual grounding not just as tasks but as signals that steer the maker's inner states.

Captioning goals encode meaning, while structure goals preserve detail. Together they push made images to match what the reading side knows. The lightweight recipe aims to recover the synergy that split designs leave unused, adding a post-training stage rather than a new architecture.
arxiv-2605-05881:
Silicon spin qubits are wired in long rails, and electrons shuttle along them to where operations happen. Arun John Moncy and seven co-authors map rotated surface codes onto that two-row railway architecture. Shuttling resolves the wiring fan-out bottleneck, but which qubits should ride, the data or the check qubits, changes the error budget.

Circuit-level noise simulations evaluate thresholds under various noise biases. Shuttling check qubits fundamentally improved thresholds. Under dephasing-biased noise, the non-CSS XZZX code beat standard variants, and a distance-7 code reached the megaquop footprint at a physical error rate of one in a thousand.
arxiv-2605-06181:
Nils Hanke, Zonglin Liu, and Olaf Stursberg approximate the limit cycles of nonlinear systems with switching affine dynamics. A limit cycle is a closed loop path a system settles into, and simple switching models make such behavior easier to model from data and analyze. Past approximations used crude two region splits or stayed in low dimensions, limiting their reach.

Their synthesis uses richer partitions of higher dimensional state spaces, with external signals added for flexibility. The method fits sampled data by numerical optimization while enforcing constraints that guarantee a globally stable limit cycle in the model. One Lyapunov function supports the approximation scheme. For reference tracking of the resulting periodic systems, they switch to multiple Lyapunov functions, which give less conservative convergence results, and examples demonstrate the approach.
arxiv-2605-06281:
Jean-Loup Dupret, Davide Gallon, and Patrick Cheridito introduce INEUS, a meshfree neural solver for partial integro-differential equations. Such equations mix local change with long range jump terms, and evaluating those integrals directly is costly, above all in high dimensions. Physics informed networks learn global solutions but pay heavily to differentiate full residuals that include the long range parts, the authors note.

INEUS swaps the explicit integral step for single jump sampling, turning the problem into a sequence of recursive regression tasks. The network still learns over the whole space time domain, yet treats long range terms far more efficiently and skips costly residual work. A contraction based proof covers convergence for linear cases. Numerical tests on varied high dimensional linear and nonlinear examples show exact, scalable solutions.
