Lead averaged 11.04 and molybdenum reached 278.67 micrograms per liter, while arsenic and uranium stayed in single digits. The authors press for safer water supplies, cleanup, and long-term study of mixed exposures in affected communities.
pmc-13301481:
Ivan Panfilov and co-authors stress test a femoral hip implant across three material choices in a 2026 engineering study. The team characterized a titanium alloy implant by nanoindentation, microscopy, and elemental analysis. They rebuilt its geometry from micro CT scans and simulated an impact modeled on an animal jumping onto the leg. Against the measured titanium they ran handbook titanium values and a cobalt chromium molybdenum alloy, a rival in joint replacement.

Under the impact loading, the cobalt alloy's load bearing capacity came out about thirty percent below the handbook titanium case and about twenty-one percent below the experimentally measured titanium. The comparison underlines that catalog stiffness values and measured properties do not tell the same story in a finite element model. pmc-13301581:
A marine-derived lung drug candidate gets its full travel diary through the rat body in a 2026 pharmacokinetic study by Xiaochen Niu and colleagues. Re-reading earlier single-dose data showed no sex gap, and seven days of daily dosing produced no pile-up of drug or metabolite. Binding, stability, and excretion studies complete a package meant to shape first human trial design.
pmc-13301781:
A torn womb during pregnancy is rare, and babies pay the highest price, Bohye Gil and colleagues report in a 2026 single-center cohort study. Among 50,185 deliveries from 2008 to mid-2024, twenty-two complete uterine ruptures occurred, an incidence of 0.044 percent. Abdominal pain, the commonest warning, also predicted trouble, urging fast action.
pmc-13302081:
Forever chemicals may bend the immune system through a shared set of genes, Katarina Baralić and colleagues argue in a 2026 in silico toxicology study. pmc-13302281:
M Dogan, C Coteli, and colleagues correlate, in a 2026 study, MRI-defined corridors through heart scar with electrical maps in patients having ablation for ventricular tachycardia. Corridor length alone independently marked that link, and most corridors reached beyond the inner heart surface into deeper layers. Outer-layer scar burden predicted rhythm recurrence during follow-up.
pmc-13302481:
When standard drugs fail stubborn obsessive-compulsive disorder, experts sometimes push doses past the guidelines, Mario Pinzi and colleagues document in a 2026 paper. A review of past evidence sits beside five hard cases from a referral clinic. Each patient had failed at least two full serotonin drug trials, clomipramine included, plus talk therapy where it was offered.

pmc-13303081:
Higher body mass tracks with nineteen cancers and against three, Eleanor L. Watts and colleagues tally in a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis. Prospective studies of twenty-five cancer types, 226 articles holding 1.5 million incident cases, were pooled and checked against earlier consensus reports. Mendelian randomization and imaging studies were reviewed alongside for support.

Associations bent by region and sex: East Asia showed stronger links for postmenopausal breast and ovarian cancers, and men for colorectal cancer. Waist size told much the same story as BMI. Genetic evidence mostly agreed, strengthening the case that adiposity itself drives the risk.
pmc-13303381:
Yanxia Zhang, Bing Zhang, and Yuemei Ding study a round RNA that drives growth in a throat cancer. Their paper is from two thousand twenty-six, with a title in Chinese in the pack. The cancer is nasopharyngeal carcinoma, which grows behind the nose. The round RNA, circFOXP1, is high in tumour tissue, while its target small RNA is low.

pmc-13304581:
Ana María Cevallos, Tomas Meraz-Tay, and Roberto Hernández review, in a 2026 paper, how veterinarians diagnose tick- and fly-borne protozoal diseases in animals. Babesiosis, theileriosis, trypanosomosis, and their relatives sicken livestock and pets worldwide, and several threaten people too. Antibody tests suit exposure screening and trade certification but struggle to separate past from active infection. DNA-based tools, from standard PCR to sequencing, supply sensitivity and species-level answers increasingly usable at the point of care. The authors close with a One Health plea for integrated surveillance across animal, human, and ecosystem health.
pmc-13306081:
Veronica Di Paolo and colleagues present in 2026 a genetic algorithm method for predicting drug interactions in horses involving the liver enzyme CYP3A. The algorithm estimated how much of each substrate depends on CYP3A and how strongly partner drugs interfere. More than ninety-six percent of predictions landed within the accepted range of half to twice the observed values. pmc-13306581:
Hadi Shammout tested whether tablet coating pigments shield a light-sensitive drug during laser marking in a 2026 study. Laser marks help fight counterfeit medicines without solvents, yet the beam may harm drugs such as nifedipine inside the tablet.

Marks were burned at four wavelengths, 193 nm, 248 nm, 532 nm and 781 nm in the listed plan, with long daylight exposure as a comparison. Results guide safer coating choice for marked tablets.
pmc-13307181:
Francisco Vale reported lasting CMV antibody oddity in a pregnant woman on immune-modulating treatment in a 2026 case account. The patient, a 39-year-old with ankylosing spondylitis, showed persistent IgM positivity and high virus levels, yet never produced the IgG switch doctors expect over two years of fertility follow-up.

During pregnancy IgM stayed positive with brief virus returns, while fetal scans stayed normal and no virus DNA appeared in amniotic fluid in reported checks. pmc-13307681:
Zicheng Liang and co-authors outline in 2026 a joint clinic and research system for gut diseases that blends Western medicine with traditional Chinese medicine. Care and lab work feed each other in a loop, so bedside notes shape study aims and study results flow back into care plans.

pmc-13307881:

pmc-13308981:

pmc-13310781:

pmc-13310981:

Emotional weakness linked the stages, shaped by each setting.
pmc-13311081:

Options disrupt wall strength, starve energy, jam transport of wall parts, enlist host defenses, and use nano carriers for delivery. pmc-13311281:

pmc-13311581:

pmc-13311681:

pmc-13311981:

pmc-13312081:

pmc-13312181:

Young ducks were then given a hormone challenge at three weeks. Stress hormone release rose more in the drug group then. Fear acts, though, showed no change from the drug.
pmc-13312481:
Ariadna Tibau and co-authors comment, in a 2026 article, on the real clinical value of cancer drugs approved in Switzerland. pmc-13312581:

pmc-13313181:

pmc-13314581:

pmc-13314781:

pmc-13314881:

pmc-13315081:

pmc-13316181:

pmc-13316281:

pmc-13316581:

pmc-13316781:

pmc-13316981:

pmc-13317381:

pmc-13317781:
Apichaya Klaikaew and co-authors compare, in a 2026 case-control study, the urine microbe mix and acidity of women with and without overactive bladder, the urgent, frequent need to urinate without infection. The bladder was long thought sterile, and its resident microbes may play a role.

Acidity matched between groups, and the overall microbe mix did not split either. Two genera, Corynebacterium and Rothia, ran more abundant in the symptom group. With small numbers, the authors frame the hints as starting points for larger, mechanistic studies.
pmc-13317981:

One tool infers exact region lengths and counts reads fast, and the second, TFEA-LE, joins those counts with DNA motif clues to name responsive switches and their likely controllers together. On p53-driven tests it beat general tools on both precision and recall, and it untangled mixed regulator responses in lung cells. pmc-13318781:
Sulian Gu and co-authors present a 2026 retrospective study of swallowing problems after severe stroke. Dysphagia is common and dangerous in this group. Records came from a neurointensive care unit at a large hospital. Admissions spanned January 2023 to August 2025.

Among 358 patients, 288 developed dysphagia, an incidence of 80.45 percent in the cohort. Five factors independently raised risk in their model. They were age 70 or older, deep brain lesion location, and a coma score of 8 or less. Mechanical ventilation and sedative use completed the list. A model built on those five factors reached an AUC of 0.864 for prediction in internal testing. The authors say outside validation is still needed before routine use.
pmc-13318981:
Sureewan Bumrungthai and colleagues present a 2026 community study in Thailand linking a gene variant to detection of human herpesvirus 6. The adjusted odds ratio was 3.21 in their model. Lower education also linked to detection, while psychological measures did not. The authors stress that long-term studies must test whether the link is causal.
pmc-13319081:
Mehdi Duyan and colleagues present a 2026 cross-sectional study of mindfulness and emotion control among female combat sports coaches. The sample held 398 women in a high-demand coaching setting. Self-report scales measured mindfulness, rumination, and control problems. Models tested whether rumination carried part of the effect.

The indirect path through it was significant, showing partial mediation. Coaches who dwelled less on negative thoughts gained extra emotional steadiness. The authors advise pairing mindfulness training with strategies aimed directly at such dwelling in coach support programmes.
pmc-13319481:
Serap BATI and Sibel KIYAK survey married women after a major quake in Türkiye in a 2026 study of death fears and plans for children. Scores were higher for women who had changed their child plans, and grief linked parts scored highest of all. Age, income, past births, house damage, and being trapped all shaped distress. Post quake care should weigh these fears.
pmc-13320281:
Bingyuan Liu and co-authors cloak a drug loaded particle in immune cell skin for stroke care in a 2026 mouse study. Restoring blood flow after a stroke clot can itself harm the brain through a burst of cell stress and swelling. Their particle packs a proven guard drug inside a tea extract and iron core, then wraps it in skin from immune scout cells that home to harm.

The wrapped particle crossed into the brain, sought the starved zone, and soaked up harmful oxygen forms while blocking fat damage in lab tests. In mice with a blocked brain artery later freed, it shrank the dead zone, cut nerve cell death and swelling, and aided movement recovery and long term survival. The design merges shield and homing in one shot.
pmc-13320381:
Joaquin Ameller and co-authors present a data set on fresh vegetable flows into Brazzaville in a 2026 survey article. Knowing where a city food comes from helps plan transport, markets, and food safety, yet such maps for this capital had not been made since the 1990s. Sellers at the main wholesale and retail markets were asked face to face about stock on one day in each of the dry and rainy seasons.

Sixteen vegetables were tracked by price, weight, and source, from farm site and region down to middle sellers where they played a part. Clean shared fields join flows to supply nodes across the chain. The set can feed studies of city food reach, market webs, and truck routes, and can be set next to like sets from other African capitals.
pmc-13321281:
Yucui Ding and colleagues review calcium overload as a way to kill cancer cells in a 2026 article. Clinical use is held back by weak tumour targeting, low build-up in tumours, and patchy mechanism knowledge.

It also surveys calcium based nano carriers paired with sound or heat based therapies for stronger joint effects. Designs that respond to the tumour setting are flagged as the next step for safer, sharper treatment.
pmc-13322181:
Jérémy Defrance and colleagues argue, in 2026, that counting second broods changes conclusions about natural selection on breeding timing in great tits. pmc-13322581:
Deep Sengupta writes a 2026 letter on anaesthesia outside the operating room for a child with Wilson's disease and autism. The case involved an 11-year-old boy weighing 32 kilograms who needed an MRI scan. Wilson's disease impairs the liver and copper handling, while autism with profound hyperactivity makes lying still for scanning impossible without deep sedation.

Published guidance, Sengupta notes, covers major surgery in Wilson's disease almost exclusively, stressing liver harm, kidney risk from copper, and odd responses to muscle relaxants. Guidance for sedation in an isolated MRI suite, above all with severe behaviour conditions added, is nearly absent. The letter presents intravenous propofol use in that gap and reviews the child's ongoing medicines.
pmc-13323181:
Riley M Boyd and colleagues measure, in 2026, how often lymphatic complications strike patients living with a Fontan circulation, the surgical rerouting used for single-ventricle hearts. These complications include fluid in the abdomen, protein loss through the gut and casts blocking the airways. Their causes and wider consequences are poorly mapped.

Affected patients were older, had their Fontan operation later and ran higher pressures in the circuit. Kidney dysfunction, clots and rhythm problems clustered with the complications. Transplant and death rates were far higher in the affected group. The authors link the pattern to raised venous pressure rather than weak heart squeezing.
pmc-13323681:
José Rodolfo Lopes de Paiva Cavalcanti and co-editors introduce a collection on the basal ganglia and their circuits, in a 2026 editorial. These deep brain nuclei, spanning striatum, pallidum, subthalamic nucleus and substantia nigra, were long cast as movement controllers alone.

Classic direct, indirect and hyperdirect pathway models still frame debate, with the direct path easing movement and the indirect path holding it back. Featured work updates those models against disorders such as Parkinson's and Huntington's disease. The editors frame the set as a step toward circuit-level treatment ideas.
pmc-13323781:
Federica Vinciguerra and co-authors tested tirzepatide for patients who regained weight after bariatric surgery or endoscopic bariatric therapy. Their 2026 observational cohort followed 34 patients, 32 after surgery and 2 after endoscopic therapy, measuring weight, body mass index categories, and side effects at starting and after 24 weeks of treatment. Side effects were confined to the gut, constipation, diarrhea, and nausea, and were generally mild, with none forcing a stop to treatment. The authors present tirzepatide as a promising nonsurgical option for this group, while noting that the evidence is preliminary and observational.
pmc-13324681:
Vladimir Aron and colleagues locate where exercise dulls pain in a 2026 experiment with healthy young men. One hard workout briefly lowers pain sensitivity, but whether the effect is body-wide or local was unclear.

Thirty-eight men aged 18 to 30 cycled for 25 minutes at strong effort or at light effort as a control. Before and after, the team tested pressure, heat, cold, and pinprick sensitivity in the worked legs and the resting arms. Hard cycling raised pressure pain thresholds only in the legs. Other measures barely moved, and hearing checks stayed flat. The pattern points to deep tissue sensors inside the working muscles as the main site of the effect.
pmc-13325081:
Rocco Malaspina and colleagues mix zinc oxide tetrapods into silk fibroin to make flexible sensing films in a 2026 materials study. Silk protein is body-friendly and breaks down safely, which suits wearable and medical devices.

After the solvent dried, the filler formed spheres, lines, or branched shapes depending on its amount in the silk matrix. pmc-13325581:
Yali Huang and ten co-authors study how metals in the blood affect the results of lab aided conception, and whether a mother's diet shifts those effects. Contact with metals may harm female fertility, but proof for these treatments is thin. The study came out in twenty twenty-six.

The team followed about four hundred women through their first treatment cycle. Blood levels of ten metals were read early in the cycle. Diet patterns came from a food survey and were sorted by a pattern method. Models weighed age, body traits, and hormone levels. Some metal links with outcomes held up after strict checks, and diet patterns changed the strength of some links, the authors report.
pmc-13327981:
Renjie Ji and a large team examine an immune checkpoint in spinal cord injury in a 2026 mouse study. Tim-3 sits on microglia, the cord's resident immune cells, and its role in post-injury inflammation was unclear. pmc-13328281:
Demet Yüksel Dal, Boran A Kilic, and Gurur Gamgam examine local brain network changes across cognitive decline in a 2026 study. Alzheimer's disease breaks links between brain regions, a disconnection pattern that may first trigger compensatory rewiring. The team measured node-level traits such as degree, strength, clustering, and centrality across disease stages.

Because the data are one-time snapshots of groups, the authors label compensation a working hypothesis needing repeat and longitudinal proof before any clinical use.
pmc-13328781:
Yong-Seok Jee writes in 2026 about how journal peer review is changing, with a focus on exercise rehabilitation. Review once acted mainly as a gate before publication, checking methods and novelty. In this field reviewers must also judge clinical value and real-world use, which makes the job broader.

Rising submission counts and demands for faster decisions now strain reviewers, editors, and publishers. Fatigue among reviewers is a growing worry, the essay notes. At the same time, open science brings calls for clearer decisions and more open debate after publication. Jee argues that review is becoming a shared duty for the research community, not just a filter before print.
pmc-13329381:
Jianyu Huang and co-authors study how a flavour compound binds to pumpkin seed protein in a 2026 report. The compound, tetramethylpyrazine, gives aroma to fermented foods but fades fast and breaks down quickly. Pumpkin seed protein was tested as a carrier that might hold and protect it.

Binding grew with dose and changed the protein shape, the team found. Light-based tests pointed to still binding driven by hydrogen bonds and weak surface forces, releasing heat as it formed. At apt levels the protein became more ordered and spread out. Computer models flagged key contact points on the protein. The mix also showed stronger antioxidant action and steadier emulsions. The authors propose the protein as a carrier for fragile flavours.
pmc-13329481:
Noah Williams and colleagues count personal costs of emergency care in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, in a 2026 study. Even under public funding, patients may pay for food, travel, and lost work. The team surveyed and interviewed people who visited four emergency departments, two rural and two urban, between March 2021 and July 2023.

Of 818 patients in the final group, 24 percent reported personal costs for a visit in the reported results. Stays of 4 hours or more raised the odds of any cost and of costs at or above 200 Canadian dollars in the adjusted models. City visits also linked to higher costs. Interviews stressed missed work and hard choices between care and daily needs.
pmc-13330481:
Quentin Marlier and colleagues test a new compound, DX243, in lab and mouse models of stroke in a 2026 study. Restoring blood flow is the only current care and reaches few patients in time. Cell models mimicked stroke stress with glutamate and with oxygen and glucose loss followed by return.

DX243 raised energy output after glutamate stress and kept neurons alive after the deprivation test in the reported results. In mice, one under-skin dose after an hour of artery blockage cut damaged brain area and preserved balance beam skill at 48 hours. Open field movement showed no clear change. The authors see repair-like promise and call for deeper preclinical and clinical work.
pmc-13330681:
Anna Carollo and colleagues write a 2026 letter on phone and video support for Parkinson patients between hospital stays. Their neuropsychology service at a hospital in Gravedona ed. Uniti, Italy, began regular remote check-ins after rehab admissions. Patients and caregivers were called to review training adherence and tackle fresh difficulties at home.

Rehab helps Parkinson care, yet structured follow-up between admissions is often missing, the letter notes. Caregivers joined calls both to clarify patient needs and to share their own strain and coping. The team reports high satisfaction, steady care continuity, and workable delivery in their summary. Remote contact can extend hospital rehab into daily life, they argue.
pmc-13331181:
Diogo Gonçalves Mesquita and team tell of two cases of postoperative spinal cord herniation. Their 2026 report notes that this very rare problem follows durotomy surgery, where failed watertight dural closure may cause pseudomeningocele growth and growing cord tethering, causing herniation and decline.

A 68-year-old man had delayed cervical cord herniation nineteen months after C5 to C7 meningioma removal, with growing limb paresthesia. Both patients healed much, with full healing in the neck case. The team stresses early freeing with sealed closure to prevent damage.
pmc-13331781:
Wareerat Prasitwiset and co-authors report a 2026 veterinary case from Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, the first documented dog infection with the parasite Leishmania martiniquensis. The dog had a small firm lump on the inner surface of its right ear, and needle sampling showed parasite forms inside cells.

pmc-13332181:

pmc-13333181:

He was referred after a failed retrieval attempt at another hospital in South India. Chest X-ray showed left lung volume loss with compensatory overinflation on the right, while CT showed an endobronchial object in the left main bronchus with lingular collapse. pmc-13333281:

pmc-13333381:

The team measured day-to-day carry-over and moving averages across activity, communication, sleep, and phone use. In depression, carry-over rose for activity and communication, strongest in later weeks of an episode, while average levels fell across activity, communication, and sleep. The authors say the two measures capture different sides of episode dynamics and need testing in bigger cohorts.
pmc-13333781:
Lluis Font-Vizcarra and Beatriz Sobrino-Díaz wrote a 2026 minireview on electrolytic cleaning as a way to strip biofilm from medical implants. Bacterial biofilms on metal surfaces shrug off antibiotics and immune attack, which makes implant infections hard to cure without removing hardware.

pmc-13334981:

About one fifth of the sample, 11,325 children, lived in states where carrying a handgun without a permit was allowed. pmc-13335981:

Combined tests and theory find a single domain wall sliding at the middle.
pmc-13336081:

pmc-13336381:

pmc-13336481:

pmc-13336881:

pmc-13337481:

pmc-13337881:

pmc-13339181:
Peng Gao and colleagues test preventive steroid dosing in newborn heart surgery in a 2026 trial. Methylprednisolone is often given to calm inflammation from the heart-lung machine, yet benefit for newborn outcomes was unclear. Clinicians assigned treatment without randomization or blinding.

Blood inflammation markers and clotting marker D-dimer were the main measures. pmc-13339281:

pmc-13339481:
Hyunsik Kim and colleagues tested in 2026 whether anxiety passes from parents to children through specific disorders or through a broad tendency toward anxiety. The team asked whether parental anxiety factors predict child anxiety broadly, specific child disorders, or early onset in childhood. Separating the pathways matters for prevention: a broad pathway points to family wide support, while specific pathways point to targeted screening. The findings help clinicians judge risk in children of anxious parents.
pmc-13339881:

A two-stage selection process using forest resampling picked stable predictors while balancing case and control traits. Several learning models were compared for accuracy. A light model from ordinary labs could flag women needing mental health checks during liver care.
pmc-13341181:

pmc-13341281:
Alexis Genaro Ortiz Altamirano and colleagues told of an obturator hernia case in 2026 in a 66 year old woman. Obturator hernias are rare. Prior belly ops biased the team toward scar band blockage, which led to first trying conservative care.

Key signs were absent, which delayed advanced scans, until CT found a right sided obturator hernia with bowel perforation. Emergency surgery followed. The case warns that obturator hernia must stay in mind for elderly thin women with blocked bowel, even when prior surgery points to scar bands.
pmc-13341481:

pmc-13342081:

Like outcomes were pooled under random-effects models with subgroup and sensitivity checks. pmc-13342181:
Moving more links to less loneliness in Yi schoolchildren, in a 2026 one-time study by Qingju Shao's team. Forms from 671 students aged 10 to 18 in Southwest China gauged activity beside anxiety, loneliness, and social anxiety, with age, sex, and school stage held in the model.

pmc-13342881:
Arlene Mitchell and co-authors describe a 2026 dataset from the Global Survey of School Meal Programs, a repeated worldwide count of school feeding work. The standardized files give policymakers and researchers a shared base for tracking programs and planning investment.
pmc-13343881:
Moaz Elsayed Abouelmagd and co-authors project Egypt's health spending and payment mix from 1995 to 2050 in a 2026 study. pmc-13344081:
Akshita Akshita and colleagues weighed stitch methods in 2026 for emergency belly surgery wound healing. pmc-13345681:
Godwin Giebel and co-authors looked in 2026 at how prescribed digital health apps for mental illness reach patients in Germany. Since 2020, people with public cover can get these apps in two ways. pmc-13345781:
Chien-Hung Chang and co-authors pool results for drug-coated balloons in narrowed brain arteries in a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis. pmc-13345881:
Gianni Bonnici and co-authors show that one macrophage type is required for the heart growth that exercise triggers in 2026. pmc-13346681:
Randriamanovontsoa Niaina Ezra and colleagues described in 2026 the pattern of liver cancer care in Toamasina, Madagascar, where international guidelines often fit poorly with local resources. pmc-13347781:
Chioma Ohajunwa, Adele Ebrahim, and Nafisa Mayat open a special issue on faith and life with a disability in Africa, in an editorial from 2026. pmc-13348181:

pmc-13349781:
Ali Shokri and colleagues assessed diet quality among older adults in Iran in a 2026 multi-source study. They combined national household survey data covering 110,765 older adults from 2019 to 2022 with two cohorts, one in Tehran and one in Birjand.

Their findings point to clear gaps in food intake for a fast-ageing population.
pmc-13349881:
Lina Kong and co-authors described high-frequency ultrasound findings for cutaneous hidrocystoma, a rare benign sweat gland cyst, in a 2026 case series. Eleven patients with cysts confirmed by tissue testing were examined by dermatologists and then scanned by experienced radiologists.

The scans recorded each lesion's site, size, shape, edges, internal echoes, blood flow, and relation to nearby tissue, and these features were matched against the tissue results. Such cysts are hard to name from appearance alone, and imaging detail can help separate them from other skin lumps before surgery. pmc-13349981:
Lorenza Cananzi and colleagues reviewed in 2026 mediastinal fat as an active player in cardiovascular disease, moving beyond the view of fat as inert padding. pmc-13350181:
Renata Pacholczak-Madej and colleagues mapped evidence in a 2026 scoping review on cell-cycle blocking drugs for adult granulosa cell tumours, a rare ovarian cancer prone to late return. Hormone treatment is also relevant because these tumours often carry hormone receivers.

Joining cycle blockers with hormone therapy is a logical next step for a cancer with few options, and the review shows how thin the clinical evidence still is.
pmc-13351081:
Meiqing Lu leads a ten-author team explaining why groundwater under the Pearl River Delta is loaded with ammonium, in a study from two thousand twenty-six. Secondary pathways shifted as the salt in the water changed. It was nitrate reduction inland, and nitrite ammonification toward the sea. pmc-13351281:
Saradiva Bilqisyah Azka and co-authors validated a DNA test for chicken in food products in a 2026 methods study. Their test targets a short stretch of a mitochondrial gene and uses quantitative PCR to detect chicken specifically, a tool for catching mislabelled meat.

pmc-13354181:
Jiang Bian and others argued in 2026 that learning health systems have stalled. The stall is not for lack of data or rules, but for lack of the base that turns that stock into steady gain. The learning health system idea dates back nearly twenty years, yet few sites run it at scale. Data alone, however rich, does not change care unless an organisation can learn from it often.

The authors propose a learning utility: the full tech, human, and social stack that converts data and AI into seen learning at the speed of care. If data are fuel and AI a new engine, learning is the electricity and the utility is the grid that delivers it. pmc-13354381:
Ibrahim Khalil leads a 2026 pooled analysis of mavacamten and exercise capacity in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Oxygen uptake, ejection fraction, and serious harms were also pooled. Extra regression and sequential checks probed moderators and result firmness.
pmc-13354481:
Bikash Pandey led a 2026 snapshot study comparing pulse oximetry with arterial blood gas oxygen saturation in heavy care people on supplemental oxygen. Accurate oxygen monitoring guides care for people with low blood oxygen, and arterial blood gas study is the gold standard. It is deep, however, while a pulse oximeter is small, handy, and non-deep.

Agreement, and any full gap between the ways, matters most when oxygen levels are borderline. The results help heavy care teams decide when a bedside reading suffices and when a blood gas test is still required.
pmc-13354781:
Jose M Ranz and Alberto Civetta traced a big growth of the male breeding secretions during placenta mammal spread, in 2026. pmc-13355281:
Timm-Jonathan Stamm and co-authors write a 2026 commentary on a urine test for cancer of the upper urinary tract. The panel caught about 92 percent of cancers but gave many false alarms, while the old cell test missed more cancers yet was rarely wrong when positive. The writers see the panel as a possible rule-out tool, with care: the study design may flatter its scores, so real clinic checks are needed.
pmc-13356081:
Andrea Marcellusi led a 2026 testing of anti-PD-(L)1 drugs for early-stage cancers in Italy, measuring health and productivity effects. The study modelled health gains and productivity results from adding these agents around surgery for early-stage cancers, with stage IIB and IIC melanoma and other indications. It translates trial efficacy into national health and economic terms. Policymakers gain estimates for funding decisions about immune care before and after surgery.
pmc-13356581:
Sabin Chaulagain and co-authors share a 2026 expert opinion on a paired diabetes drug tablet, glimepiride plus metformin, in Nepal, where type 2 diabetes is rising fast. Gains in blood sugar control were marked, and newly diagnosed patients may benefit most. Risks include low blood sugar and weight gain, so the panel stresses personal dose tuning and regular follow-up.
pmc-13356781:
Vu Bui and colleagues measured surgical risks for transplant recipients undergoing lumbar spine fusion, in a 2026 propensity-matched cohort study. Over 400,000 Americans live with a functioning solid organ transplant, and more of them now need spine surgery. The findings call for tailored risk counseling and team-based perioperative care for this high-risk group.
pmc-13357081:
Qiqiang Huang led growth of a SEER-based living forecast model for poorly and mixed colorectal neuroendocrine neoplasms, in 2026. These rare, aggressive tumours lack personal prognostic testing, and usual staging captures too little of their heterogeneity. A dedicated model could guide advice and care intensity.

People diagnosed from 2000 to 2019 were drawn from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results bank, randomly split for model growth and internal validation. Multivariable signs of living were joined into a usable model. Doctors gain a tool for estimating single prognosis in a rare cancer where staging alone misleads.
pmc-13358481:
Jia Sun led a 2026 single-centre study of valve choice for aortic valve swap in people aged fifty to sixty-five. pmc-13359881:
Sofoklis Stavros and co-authors review melatonin beyond sleep in a 2026 paper. Melatonin is the night hormone that sets the body clock. pmc-13361181:
Yisheng Dong and others used deep learning inverse design for phase-change changeable THz devices, in 2026. The plan creates devices that change their response on demand. Communications builders gain a design tool for THz hardware with built-in body-layer security.
pmc-13362181:
Wenjun Meng and co-authors review pain caused by radiation therapy for head and neck cancer in a 2026 paper. This pain is among the most common and wearing side effects of treatment. pmc-13364181:
Jixing Guan, Junyu An, and Guisheng Liao present a 2026 study on imaging moving, uncooperative targets with MIMO millimeter-wave radar for security screening. pmc-13364281:

pmc-13372681:

pmc-13374081:
Salvador Morales-Conde and colleagues report experience with a laparoscopic technique for complex abdominal hernias in a 2026 study. pmc-13374381:

pmc-13375581:

pmc-13377581:

pmc-13378881:

pmc-13378981:

Follow-up checks in cell and animal models supported the findings, offering possible new targets.
pmc-13382081:

pmc-13382581:

pmc-13383281:

pmc-13383381:

pmc-13383481:

pmc-13385381:

pmc-13386681:

pmc-13386881:

pmc-13388581:

pmc-13388981:
